feature: Play starts at once on a 50 track edit
summary: Space on the 50 track edit moves the picture within about a twentieth of a second, at rest and right after a jump, where it used to stand still for 230 to 880 ms.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed. Your copy of the 50 track edit: File > Open (Cmd-Shift-G) ~/Library/Caches/Photonz Reference Edit/Photonz Dev/Reference Edit 50 tracks.photonz. Measured in the probe, worst of three, before and after on the same Mac. First moving picture after Space, two seconds at rest at 0:10 / 0:30 / 0:58: before 632 / 258 / 877 ms, after 66 / 58 / 67. Space the moment a jump's picture is in: before 694 / 600 / 861, after 56 / 50 / 50. Half a second after a jump: before 642 / 392 / 858, after 50 / 50 / 50, and at 1:02 with ten recordings up 775 before, 83 after. Frames dropped in the first 3 seconds at rest: 0:10 17 before, 0 after; 0:58 24 before, 0 after. The walk is play-starts-at-once-on-a-wide-edit-walk; Scripts/perf/speed-walk.sh --wide records the same numbers.

try.do: Open Reference Edit 50 tracks.photonz with File > Open.
Click the ruler at 0:10, wait two seconds, press Space.
Press Space to stop, click the ruler at 0:58, press Space as soon as the picture is there.
Stop, click at 1:02, where ten recordings play, and press Space.
Stop and start with Space a few times in a row without moving the playhead.
Click somewhere new and press Space in the same instant, to see the one case that still waits.
Open the 6 minute reference edit in Photonz Dev with the button below and press Space: it starts as it did.

evaluate: Does Space feel immediate at 0:10, 0:58 and 1:02?
Does any clip flash, or show a picture from another moment, as play starts?
Is the sound in step from the first moment?
When you press Space in the same instant as a jump, would you rather wait a third of a second, or see it play with a few small clips still missing?
rough: Space in the very same instant as a jump still waits 230 to 545 ms (545 to 870 before): each clip has to be decoded up from its key frame, which the Mac's decoder cannot do for six clips in a tenth of a second. It waits for the big clips and half of all of them, keeping the picture that was up.
With ten recordings up in that case, up to four small clips join as late as 0.6 s after play starts. Each is left out until its own frame is there, never shown from another time.
Started at 1:02 with nothing waited for, two small clips were missing for 1.8 s, so it waits for half.
A jump while paused still draws the new place piece by piece as each clip is read. That was so before. Filed as its own task, a-jump-on-a-wide-edit-shows-its-picture-whole-an.
Frames held ready at rest take about 220 MB where ten recordings are up, and one percent of a core. They are let go after two minutes at rest, and when the Mac is short of memory.
Right after a minute of editing the same starts read 79 to 91 ms. The whole edit played three times dropped 0 of 10,908 frames; one run right after all the other measures dropped 3.
100 tracks: 94 to 109 ms at rest, 74 to 78 after a jump. That edit is not held to this bar yet.
